comparison: Both evaluate claims about PCNA SUMOylation and telomere elongation in elg1Δ (C43-C57). OpenEval finds the genetic and overexpression data SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing significant doubt about the mechanistic interpretation that SUMO-PCNA acts as a positive signal for telomerase activation, noting that pol30-RR strains have normal telomere length.

Both evaluate epistasis between ELG1 and STN1 (C64-C66). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers agree this is SUPPORTED, accepting the double mutant analysis as solid evidence that these proteins work in the same pathway.

Both evaluate physical interactions between Elg1 and CST components (C67-C69, C85). Both rate as SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers noting these interactions as a strength of the paper. OpenEval also includes additional claims about SIM mutations and differential interactions (C74-C77, C83-C84) that overlap with peer R4.

Partial overlap on YTH data showing domain-specific interactions (C74-C77, C83-C84). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R3 covers broader interaction data while peer R4 focuses specifically on SIM-dependent interactions.

Both evaluate differential SUMOylation dependencies for Elg1-Cdc13 versus Elg1-Stn1 interactions (C88-C100). Both rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the YTH and co-IP data demonstrating PCNA-dependent versus PCNA-independent interactions.

Both evaluate the requirement for Elg1 catalytic activity and PCNA unloading for Cdc13 interaction (C101-C114, C123-C125). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing doubt about the mechanistic interpretation that the interaction is indirect and activity-dependent.

Both evaluate Cdc13 SUMOylation requirement (C121-C122). Both rate as SUPPORTED, accepting this as one of the conditions necessary for Elg1-Cdc13 interaction. OpenEval R6 also covers broader requirements (C117-C125) that overlap with peer R6.

Partial overlap on the three requirements for Elg1-Cdc13 interaction (C123-C125). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN about the mechanistic interpretation of these requirements.

Both evaluate cell cycle timing of Elg1-Stn1 interaction (C128-C129, C131-C132). Both rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the co-IP and ChIP data showing late S-phase interaction correlated with telomerase activity timing.

Both evaluate reduced Stn1-Cdc13 interaction in elg1Δ (C134-C135). Both rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the co-IP data showing Elg1's role in CST complex assembly, though peer reviewers question broader mechanistic implications.
Minimal overlap on C133 (ChIP data). OpenEval R8 focuses on functional consequences while peer R12 focuses on domain mapping. Both accept the underlying experimental data.

Both evaluate the integrated model of PCNA unloading and CST assembly (C115-C116, C136-C153, C164, C167-C168). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting speculative elements, while peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, explicitly stating the model is not convincingly demonstrated and that pol30-RR data contradicts necessity claims.

Both evaluate the two-mode interpretation reconciling PCNA SUMOylation requirements (C157-C161). Both rate UNCERTAIN, with OpenEval noting the interpretation relies on analogy and is not directly tested, while peer reviewers use pol30-RR normal telomere data to question the model's necessity.
Partial overlap on domain mapping (C127). Both rate as SUPPORTED, accepting YTH data characterizing Elg1-NTD and Stn1 C-terminus interaction domains.
OpenEval R11 covers structural organization and domain mapping (C70-C73, C81-C82, C126-C127) while peer R4 covers SIM-dependent interactions. Both accept the YTH domain mapping data as SUPPORTED.
OpenEval R12 evaluates background/context claims (C1-C37, C50, C62, C154-C156, C162-C163, C165-C166) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval R13 evaluates core novel findings from abstract/introduction (C6-C8, C38-C42) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these summary claims, though peer reviewers evaluate the underlying data supporting these claims in other results.
